_comment: Colorado Springs v3 — source-led (coverage-first) re-research of the Colorado Springs, CO MSA (El Paso + Teller). Separate config and separate batch tag from scripts/metros/colorado-springs.json and colorado-springs-addendum.json, on the lancaster-v3 precedent: both 2026-08-03 imports stay immutable and this carries its own one-statement rollback handle. Same metro_area, so the public URL /courts/in/colorado-springs is unchanged. NOT YET IMPORTED — read-only projection only.
_artifact_loss_premise_is_WRONG_and_here: The rescue was commissioned on the premise that metro-research/colorado-springs/ was destroyed by the 2026-08-03 `git clean -fdx` and was unrecoverable. THE MAIN BATCH ARTIFACT IS NOT LOST. `metro-research/colorado-springs/colorado-springs-candidates.json` exists on disk and is byte-identical (md5 e45db0e4d90632f5e8099855f82fa099) to `general-ai-team/court-verifier/output/colorado-springs-2026-08-03/pipeline-candidates.json`, which was never touched by the clean because it lives in a DIFFERENT REPOSITORY. The `git clean` ran in the Joinzer checkout; the court-verifier output tree is in general-ai-team. The artifact's own metadata names that generator ('Local generator: general-ai-team court-verifier/output/colorado-springs-2026-08-03/build-workbook.mjs'), so the recovery path was recorded inside the very file that was declared missing. CONSEQUENCE: colorado-springs-2026-08-03 can run EVERY stage today, including --stage=publish for its 11 held rows; it was never structurally blocked, only believed to be. The ADDENDUM artifact IS genuinely absent (metro-research/colorado-springs-addendum/ does not exist and general-ai-team has no addendum generator), so colorado-springs-addendum-2026-08-03 remains blocked for its single held row (pines-and-paddles). Both 2026-08-03 configs still carry an `_artifact_lost` block asserting total loss; that block is now false for the main batch and should be corrected in its own edit, not silently here.

_disposition_buckets._question: A venue found by this pass that already exists as a HELD DRAFT collides on slug (slug is globally unique), and the reconcile mechanism is unusable because reconciles[] mandates osm_id and these rows have none. Three dispositions were possible per row. This is the count and the reasoning.
_disposition_buckets._arithmetic: 29 pre-existing rows = 17 (a) + 11 (c) + 1 retire. The 7 in (b) are net-new venues with no pre-existing row and are the ONLY rows this artifact contains.
_disposition_buckets._a_reasoning: All 17 published rows are left byte-for-byte untouched and are absent from the artifact entirely. 15 of the 17 were independently re-confirmed this pass against a non-aggregator source; the remaining 2 are flagged under _live_rows_that_did_not_hold_up below. Excluding is strictly safer than importing: it keeps this batch a clean INSERT against a disjoint slug set, so `update facility_listings set status='draft' where source='colorado-springs-v3-2026-08-05'` reverses the whole thing without touching a published URL.
_disposition_buckets._b_reasoning: 7 genuinely new venues, each with no pre-existing row and each carrying a controlling-entity or operator source. These are the only rows here.
_disposition_buckets._c_reasoning: 11 held drafts are REAL venues whose row already exists and whose deficiency is sourcing, naming or a missing address — not absence. Re-importing them would collide on slug; excluding them alone would leave the defect in place. What they need is a keyed UPDATE on the existing row, which is a separate gated slice and deliberately NOT part of this import. Per-row detail in _keyed_update_slice.
_disposition_buckets._retire_reasoning: colorado-springs-pickleball-the-warehouse-colorado-springs-co has NO citable non-aggregator source. Its operator domain cspickleball.com is now a gambling/battery-affiliate spam site — the 2026-08-03 note that the 'operator domain is repurposed' is confirmed and has not reverted. Its name_source_url is a pickleheads.com aggregator URL, which is an ADR-14 violation that is currently latent only because the row has no coordinate; it would trip the abort the moment anyone geocoded it. Under the methodology's 'a venue you cannot cite does not go in the list', it should be retired rather than repaired.

_keyed_update_slice._note: NOT part of this import. Recorded here so the findings survive between sessions, exactly as the 2026-08-03 config's _v3_reresearch_findings block intended.
_keyed_update_slice.cheyenne-mountain-country-club-colorado-: MISIDENTIFIED ENTITY, not merely under-sourced. There is no separate club called 'Cheyenne Mountain Country Club'. The real venue at that location is The Country Club of Colorado at Cheyenne Mountain Resort, 125 E Clubhouse Dr, Colorado Springs, CO 80906 (ccofcolorado.com / cheyennemountain.com), which has 8 dedicated outdoor pickleball courts and 1 indoor. So the row's identity citation (openstreetmap.org/way/1470162223) and its coordinate (derived from way/220300890, a DIFFERENT OSM object) were both standing in for a name that does not designate an entity. The venue IS real and IS a pickleball venue — the fix is rename + address + operator source, not retirement.
_keyed_update_slice.wasson-high-school-colorado-springs-co: NAME DESIGNATES A SCHOOL THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. Wasson High School closed at the end of the 2012-13 year. The site at 2115 Afton Way is now the Roy J. Wasson Academic Campus (rjwac.d11.org), a District 11 alternative/adult-education campus — which is why no D11 source could be found to confirm 'Wasson High School' in the 2026-08-03 pass. The courts are real (pppall lists 6: 2 dual-striped plus 4 needing portable nets). Fix is rename to the current designation plus a d11.org source; access_type `school` remains correct.
_keyed_update_slice.portal-park-colorado-springs-co: ADDRESS CONFLICT WITH THE CONTROLLING ENTITY. The row carries 1216 Devonshire St (from pppall); the City of Colorado Springs' own neighborhood-parks page gives Portal Park as 3535 N. Hancock Ave. (N Hancock Ave. and Manchester St.), 10.6 acres, four tennis courts. The stored coordinate 38.8847,-104.8013 sits at the Hancock/Manchester location, i.e. the coordinate follows the CITY address and the address column follows the club. Fix is to adopt the city address and re-source; the coordinate appears already correct.
_keyed_update_slice.westmoor-park-colorado-springs-co: NULL ADDRESS, RECOVERABLE. City neighborhood-parks page gives 3315 Water St. (Chambers Dr. and Westmoor Pl.), 6.6 acres, tennis courts. (Aggregators say 3359 Water St — prefer the city's 3315.) Fix is address + city source.
_keyed_update_slice.glen-park-palmer-lake-co: NULL ADDRESS, RECOVERABLE, AND A REAL MUNICIPAL SOURCE EXISTS. The Town of Palmer Lake publishes 'Glen Park Pickleball/Tennis Court Rules (court #2)' as a town meeting document on mccmeetingspublic.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net — the SAME host as the citation already carried by the live centennial-park-palmer-lake-co row — and palmerlakecolorado.org's recreation page names Glen Park's tennis courts as used for pickleball. Address is Lovers Lane, Palmer Lake, CO 80133 (no house number is published; do not invent one). This retires the 'Town of Palmer Lake publishes nothing on Glen Park' finding from 2026-08-03.
_keyed_update_slice.windmill-mesa-park-colorado-springs-co: NO COORDINATE, AND ITS CONTROLLING ENTITY IS NOW IDENTIFIED. The park is operated by Widefield School District 3's parks and recreation department, not by the City or the County — which is why the 2026-08-03 pass found the 'Widefield district site 404s on its parks pages' and left ownership unestablished. Address 4610 Fencer Rd, Security-Widefield/Colorado Springs, CO 80911. Fix is a geocode plus a wsd3 source.
_keyed_update_slice.bonforte-park-colorado-springs-co: CONFIRMED BY THE CITY, contrary to the 2026-08-03 note that the City 'actively contradicts' it. The City's neighborhood-parks page lists Bonforte Park at 2323 N. Wahsatch Ave. with two tennis courts; the City's tennis-and-pickleball page simply does not enumerate every dual-striped court. pppall confirms pickleball on those courts. Fix is to re-source name_source_url from the (venue-less) tennis-and-pickleball page to the neighborhood-parks page.
_keyed_update_slice.banning-lewis-ranch-colorado-springs-co: CONTROLLING-ENTITY SOURCE FOUND. banninglewisranch.com/life-here/amenities/ (the community's own site) confirms pickleball courts at the Northtree Ranch House. access_type `hoa` is correct — resident access. Fix is to replace the pppall citation with the community source.
_keyed_update_slice.wildflower-park-colorado-springs-co: UNRESOLVED CONFLICT — DO NOT PUBLISH YET. pppall lists 1 dual-striped tennis court with pickleball lines at 980 Nolte Dr West. The City's own neighborhood-parks entry for Wildflower Park (21.9 acres) lists baseball, soccer, basketball/in-line skate, picnic shelter and playground — and NO tennis court at all. One of the two is wrong about the court's existence. This is the only held row this pass could neither confirm nor clear, and it should stay held until someone resolves it.
_keyed_update_slice.springs-pickleball-west-colorado-springs: REAL, well-sourced (operator springspickleball.com), blocked only on coordinate precision — 780 Vondelpark Dr resolves to the road band across all rungs. Pure geocode problem, unchanged by this pass.
_keyed_update_slice.pines-and-paddles-pickleball-club-colora: REAL, well-sourced (operator pinesandpaddles.com, which self-describes as the Black Forest indoor pickleball club), blocked only on coordinate precision at 8483 Burgess Rd. Pure geocode problem. NOTE: this is the one held row whose batch (the addendum) is still genuinely artifact-blocked, so it cannot publish through its original batch even after a re-geocode.

_live_rows_that_did_not_hold_up._note: The brief asked plainly whether the 17 currently live rows hold up. 14 do — each independently re-confirmed this pass against a controlling entity or operator page. THREE do not, and one of those three is serious enough to warrant unpublishing. This config does not touch any of them; they are recorded for a decision.
_live_rows_that_did_not_hold_up.big-house-pickleball-colorado-springs-co: *** THE VENUE IS CLOSED AND WE ARE PUBLISHING IT AS OPEN. *** Its own operator site thebighousepickleball.com carries a banner reading 'BHPB CLOSED'. The row is live, published, `source_verified`, access_type private, at 3785 Interpark Dr — and it cites that same operator page, which now announces the closure. This is the single most serious finding against the live set: not a weak citation but an actively wrong fact on a published page. Recommend unpublishing (status -> draft) in the keyed-UPDATE slice, ahead of every other item in it. Note this row came from the ADDENDUM batch, whose artifact IS genuinely lost, so it cannot be corrected by re-running that batch — it needs a direct keyed UPDATE.
_live_rows_that_did_not_hold_up.downtown-ymca-colorado-springs-co: PICKLEBALL ACTIVITY NOT SUPPORTED BY THE CITED SOURCE. ppymca.org's pickleball programme page names only YMCA at First & Main and Briargate YMCA. The Downtown YMCA's OWN branch page (ppymca.org/location/downtown-ymca/, which is what this row cites) lists 2 indoor pools, racquetball courts, full gymnasiums and basketball courts — and no pickleball. The row is published as `source_verified` on a source that does not state the claim. Gym-floor play may well happen there, but this needs a real citation or the row should come down.
_live_rows_that_did_not_hold_up.peak-pickleball-colorado-springs-co: COURT COUNT LIKELY WRONG. The live row says 24. The operator is described consistently by independent secondary sources as having 16 courts. The venue, address and identity are not in question; only the number is, and court_count is not a publish-gate field.

_envelope_comment: Copied verbatim from scripts/metros/colorado-springs.json, which derived it 2026-08-03 from the Colorado Springs MSA COUNTY LIST (El Paso + Teller), not from an observed bounding box. Same metro, same counties, so re-deriving it would be a chance to introduce a difference and no chance to improve one. All 7 researched venues sit inside it.
msa: Colorado Springs, CO (El Paso and Teller counties)
_reconcile_comment: EMPTY BY NECESSITY, NOT BY CHOICE. reconciles[] mandates an osm_id and asserts exactly one live row carries it. Every colorado-springs-2026-08-03 and addendum row has osm_id NULL except the two that were themselves reconciled onto OSM drafts in that run, and neither of those is a venue this pass rediscovered as new. The mechanism is therefore unusable for this metro, which is precisely why the 11 improvable held rows are routed to a keyed-UPDATE slice instead.
_exclude_comment: EMPTY. Unlike lancaster-v3, this artifact contains ONLY net-new venues — every pre-existing row is absent from the grid rather than present-and-excluded. That is the safer shape here because the exclude validator aborts on any key it cannot find in the artifact, and because 29 pre-existing rows would have made the grid mostly a re-transcription of the database, which is the circularity the 2026-08-05 owner ruling warned against.
_expected_publish_comment: NOT YET AUTHORED — deliberately withheld until --stage=project has produced a projection, exactly as lancaster-v3 did. reportExpected says in as many words 'Fix the pipeline. Do NOT edit the expectation to match the output.' Authoring this block before the projection exists would make it a guess to be corrected; authoring it after, from a row-by-row owner review, makes it the deliberate-release mechanism ADR-17 intends. THIS CONFIG MUST NOT BE RUN PAST --stage=project UNTIL THE OWNER LOCKS THIS BLOCK.

workbook.source_description: Source-led web research, Colorado Springs CO MSA (El Paso + Teller counties), 2026-08-05 (v3 coverage-first methodology) — no workbook and no Google Sheet; the tab grid was authored directly
